 Rahm edges ahead of Hatton & McIlroy in Abu Dhabi 
 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Jon Rahm has not won an individual tournament outside of the LIV tour since the 2023 Masters
 By Craig Nelson BBC Sport Journalist Published 7 November 2026 
 Abu Dhabi Championship third-round leaderboard 
 -18 J Rahm (Spa); -17 T Hatton (Eng), F Laporta (Ita); -16 R McIlroy (NI); -15 A Scott (Aus); -14 M Jordan (Eng), D Puig (Spa)
 Selected others: -12 S Bairstow (Eng), N Kimsey (Eng); -11 T Fleetwood (Eng), E Ferguson (Sco), A Sullivan (Eng); -9 A Rai (Eng); -8 E Chacarra (Spa), M Wallace (Eng); -1 P Reed (US) 
 Full leaderboard 
 Jon Rahm has a one-shot lead going into the final round of the Abu Dhabi Championship but Ryder Cup team-mates Tyrrell Hatton and Rory McIlroy are in close contention. 
 The 31-year-old Spaniard shared the overnight lead with Italy's Francesco Laporta and fellow former LIV player Hatton, but moved clear of them both with a six-under-par 66 at Yas Links on Saturday.
 Hatton and Laporta both carded a 67, as did McIlroy, who goes into the final round in fourth place on 16 under. 
 Rahm, who said recently that he does not know what 2027 holds after quitting the LIV tour, is aiming for a first solo tournament triumph since winning the Masters in 2023.
 Reigning Masters champion McIlroy remains in hot pursuit, however, after bouncing back in spectacular fashion since being given a two-shot penalty in the opening round for improving his lie before taking a chip shot. 
 The six-time major winner hit 11 birdies in a second-round 63 and another eight in his third round, but a double bogey six at the par-four 10th - and another dropped shot at the 17th - left McIlroy two shots off the lead. 
 And he acknowledges that it will take something special on the final day to reel in Rahm and co. 
 "There are low ones [scores] out there and I am going to have to shoot a low one - something in the mid to low 60s - to get it done tomorrow and that will be the goal," said McIlroy. 
 Hatton, meanwhile, is looking forward to going head-to-head again with Rahm after playing alongside the two-time major champion, and Laporta, in Saturday's final group.
 All three will play together once again on Sunday. 
 "Obviously final group tomorrow there's a lot to play for," said Hatton, who briefly moved level with Rahm at the top of the leaderboard in the third round after holing his seventh birdie of the day on the 14th. 
 "Naturally we are going to want to beat each other. Hopefully I can get off to a good start and put him under some pressure."
 Rahm, who is chasing his first win in the Abu Dhabi Championship, responded well after being put under pressure by Hatton on Saturday. 
 He reclaimed the outright lead on the 15th with a superb, curling 20-foot birdie putt and came close to extending his advantage at the last, just coming up short with another birdie chance as he finished without a single dropped shot.
 Laporta also produced a bogey-free round to keep pace with the field's big hitters as the 36-year-old, who shot 10 under par to claim a first-round lead, bids for a first title on the DP World Tour. 
 Elsewhere, Australian Adam Scott remained bogey-free for the tournament after three rounds and moved up to fifth place on 15 under with a 66. 
 And Englishman Matthew Jordan is a shot further back, alongside Spain's David Puig, after a third-round 69.
